Chapter.Content: 12 — Transactions, recovery, and safe project boundaries
Reading map · Previous chapter · Next chapter

Interactive tools need edits that can be undone and projects that can be reopened after failure. This chapter makes mutation transactional and treats paths, packages, backups, and atomic publication as security and recovery contracts.
By the end: Design undo/redo, save recovery, path validation, and package publication so partial failure cannot silently corrupt authored work.
Recall question: Which state is authoritative before and after a failed save, and how does the system prove that the published project is complete?

Imported targets describe external artifacts; aliases provide a stable name

A CMake target is a named node in the build graph, with properties describing its sources, output and usage requirements. An imported target describes an artifact built outside this CMake build. It creates no compile/archive rule for that artifact, but consumers can still inherit its declared include paths, definitions and link requirements. An alias gives the same target another name. It does not copy properties or create a wrapper library; later changes to the real target remain visible through the alias.

This exercise uses CMake 3.18’s documented behavior. A non-GLOBAL imported target is visible in its declaring directory and descendants. CMake 3.18 permits an alias of that imported target, with matching directory visibility. An alias cannot itself be aliased, installed or exported, and cannot be the target whose properties are modified. Modify the real target; there is no requirement that all such modifications precede creation of the alias.
A complete project with an externally produced archive

Create the files below under tools/labs/cmake_imported_alias/, or use the saved copy in the vault. The vendor source is included solely so this exercise can produce its own stand-in archive before CMake runs. The CMake build then treats that archive exactly as an outside artifact: it builds only the consumer. No package download or third-party library is required.
Chapter.Code:
# STATIC describes the external archive; IMPORTED means CMake will not build it. add_library(Vendor::Math STATIC IMPORTED) set_target_properties(Vendor::Math PROPERTIES IMPORTED_LOCATION "${VENDOR_MATH_LIBRARY}" INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/include" INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "VENDOR_MATH_IMPORTED=1" )
# Alias supplies this project with a stable name. It remains the same target. add_library(Project::Math ALIAS Vendor::Math) # An alias does not copy properties. Later changes to Vendor::Math are # observed through Project::Math too; modify the real target, not the alias.
# Both imported target and its alias are visible in this child directory. add_subdirectory(consumer)

if(NOT TARGET Vendor::Math OR NOT TARGET Project::Math) message(FATAL_ERROR "Imported target and alias must be visible below deps/") endif() add_executable(imported_consumer main.cpp) # Linking the alias carries its location and include/definition usage requirements. target_link_libraries(imported_consumer PRIVATE Project::Math)

# The imported target was not GLOBAL; sibling directories cannot see it. if(TARGET Vendor::Math OR TARGET Project::Math) message(FATAL_ERROR "non-GLOBAL imported target leaked outside deps/") endif() message(STATUS "PASS: non-GLOBAL imported target and alias are directory-scoped")
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18) project(ExpectedFailure LANGUAGES CXX) add_executable(missing_target main.cpp) target_link_libraries(missing_target PRIVATE Missing::Target)
Chapter.Content: Read the dependency graph, then run it

The imported name and alias are declared in deps/. Its consumer is a descendant, so both names resolve there. The root’s scope_probe/ is a sibling, so neither non-GLOBAL name resolves there. Linking Project::Math carries the archive location, header directory and VENDOR_MATH_IMPORTED definition. The consumer never receives a hand-written include flag or macro outside the target interface, and its compile-time check fails if that interface is lost.

For independent siblings that need the dependency, declare it in their common parent, intentionally use an imported GLOBAL target, or consume a package configuration that defines the target in the required scope. An alias created where the real target is invisible does not repair visibility. The :: name is also useful: an unresolved namespaced dependency raises a configure/generate error instead of being treated as an ordinary raw linker name.
From the example’s directory, produce the archive outside the CMake graph and build the consumer. These shell comments explain which owner performs each step:
Chapter.Code:
# The host compiler and archiver act as the external vendor for this small demo. c++ -std=c++11 -Ideps/include -c deps/vendor_math.cpp -o /tmp/vendor_math.o ar rcs /tmp/libvendor_math.a /tmp/vendor_math.o
# IMPORTED_LOCATION receives an absolute path to that already-existing archive. cmake -S . -B /tmp/imported-alias-build -DVENDOR_MATH_LIBRARY=/tmp/libvendor_math.a cmake --build /tmp/imported-alias-build /tmp/imported-alias-build/deps/consumer/imported_consumer
# This independent negative project must fail for Missing::Target, not a compiler error. cmake -S negative -B /tmp/imported-alias-negative
Chapter.Content: Worked solution and expected results. The positive project reports that the imported target and alias are directory-scoped, compiles the consumer with its inherited header path and definition, links the prebuilt archive, and returns zero. The negative project fails during configuration/generation because Missing::Target is not defined. A nonzero return alone is insufficient evidence: inspect the diagnostic to confirm the intended failure. If the positive consumer cannot find the header, inspect INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES; if its macro check fails, inspect INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS; if linking fails, verify the archive’s absolute path, architecture and symbol definition.

The solution to making the target visible to a sibling is a scope change at the shared dependency declaration, not a duplicate archive or an alias of an invisible target. If a dependency’s requirements are wrong, update the real imported target; the alias remains another spelling of it.

A static archive uses IMPORTED_LOCATION. A Windows shared-library package may need both IMPORTED_IMPLIB for the link-time import library and IMPORTED_LOCATION for the runtime DLL. A header-only imported INTERFACE target has no compiled artifact. Multiple configurations may require configuration-specific locations. Those are distinct package contracts; this static host example does not test every platform layout.

Source policy: the CMake 3.18 add_library reference, target_link_libraries, and IMPORTED_LOCATION define the behavior used here. The completed lab verifies this one project under the recorded installed toolchain, not every CMake generator or vendor SDK.
